definitions.explanation: A familiar term for addressing or referring to one's older sister. Less formal than お姉さん.
An informal way to address or refer to a young woman, typically a waitress, shop attendant, or unfamiliar woman who appears to be in her twenties to thirties.

examples.japanese: {姉|ねえ}さん、⟦{手伝|てつだ}って→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧。
うち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{姉|ねえ}さん⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧だ。
examples.english: My older sister is good at cooking.

examples.japanese: ⟦{隣|となり}→隣：01003_tonari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{姉|ねえ}さん⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}して→挨拶する：01797_aisatsusuru⟧⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: The older girl next door always greets me.

examples.japanese: {姉|ねえ}さん、お⟦{勘定|かんじょう}→勘定：02582_kanjou⟧。
⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧{姉|ねえ}さん、{綺麗|きれい}だな。
⟦{市場|いちば}→市場：01803_ichiba⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{姉|ねえ}さん⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧かけられて、⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一匹|いっぴき}→一匹：08930_ippiki⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: A woman at the market called out to me, and I ended up buying a fish.

notes:
A less formal variant of お{姉|ねえ}さん, dropping the honorific お. The kanji {姉|ねえ} is used for the family relationship meaning, though the word is often written in hiragana.

USAGE:
As a family term (sense 1), {姉|ねえ}さん is casual and familiar — used within the family or among close acquaintances. As an address term (sense 2), it sounds somewhat old-fashioned or working-class, commonly heard in markets, traditional shops, and informal settings. In modern usage, sense 2 can sound overly familiar and is less common among younger speakers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- うち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{姉|ねえ}さん — my older sister (casual)
- ⟦{隣|となり}→隣：01003_tonari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{姉|ねえ}さん — the older girl/woman next door
- お{姉|ねえ}さん — older sister; young lady (politer form)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{姉|ねえ}さん — older sister; young lady (politer, more standard)
- ⟦{姉|あね}→姉：00571_ane⟧ — older sister (humble/neutral, used when speaking about one's own sister to others)
- {姐|ねえ}さん — older woman (gang/yakuza connotation or traditional arts)
